references.text: [ref:5 Mos 8:3|Deut 8:3] speaks of how man does not live by bread alone, but by every word that comes from the mouth of God. In John 4:34 Jesus expresses the same principle: spiritual nourishment – obedience to God's will – is more important than physical food.
In [ref:Matt 26:39|Matt 26:39] Jesus prays in Gethsemane: "not as I will, but as you will." This shows the same submission to the Father's will that Jesus expresses in John 4:34.
In [ref:Joh 5:30|John 5:30] Jesus says: "I do not seek my own will, but the will of him who sent me." This is a parallel to John 4:34, where Jesus declares that his food is to do the Father's will.

In [ref:Joh 6:38|John 6:38] Jesus says: "For I have come down from heaven not to do my own will but the will of him who sent me." This expresses the same theme of Jesus' total obedience to the Father.

In [ref:Joh 17:4|John 17:4] Jesus says to the Father: "I have glorified you on earth and finished the work you gave me to do." The expression "to finish his work" (τελειώσω αὐτοῦ τὸ ἔργον) in 4:34 points directly forward to this completion.

In [ref:Joh 19:30|John 19:30] Jesus says on the cross: "It is finished!" (Τετέλεσται). This is the final fulfillment of the work Jesus refers to in John 4:34 – doing the Father's will and completing his task.
In [ref:Hebr 10:7-9|Heb 10:7-9] Psalm 40 is quoted about Christ coming to do God's will. This willingness to do the Father's will is the central theme in John 4:34.

In [ref:Sal 40:9|Ps 40:8] the psalmist says: "To do your will, my God, is my delight, and your law is within my heart." This is a prophetic text about the Messiah who finds his joy in doing God's will, as Jesus expresses in John 4:34.
In [ref:Joh 8:29|John 8:29] Jesus says: "He who sent me is with me. He has not left me alone, for I always do what pleases him." This underscores Jesus' constant obedience to the Father's will.

In [ref:Fil 2:8|Phil 2:8] Christ is described as being obedient to death, even death on a cross. This obedience expresses the same thing Jesus says in John 4:34 – doing the Father's will and completing his work.
